newsitem.title: USA: American Financial to cut costs, reorganize.
newsitem.headline: American Financial to cut costs, reorganize.

text.p: American Financial Group Inc said Wednesday it is proposing steps to cut corporate expenses and reorganize as a holding company for two majority-owned subsidiaries.

The plan will affect American Financial Corp, in which it owns all of the common stock and 79 percent of the voting equity securities, and American Financial Enterprises Inc, in which it owns approximately 83 percent of the common stock.

Under the proposal, American Financial Corp would merge with a wholly-owned subsidiary. Holders of the company's Series and G preferred stock, which represent 21 percent of the company's voting securities, would receive $21.50 and $10.50 per share in cash, respectively.
All Series F record holders on May 15 will be paid the $.90 semi-annual dividend on June 3, it said.

In a tax-free alternative, holders of the both preferred stock will have the option to receive shares of new AFC preferred stock that would also hold about 21 percent of the voting power of AFC after the proposed merger.
The proposal values the two classes of preferred stock series at a total of $276 million, it said.

American Financial Group is also proposing a merger deal with American Financial Etnerprises in which all publicly held shares of the latter would be exchanged, at the holder's option, for common shares of American Financial Group on a one-for-one basis, or $37 per share in cash.
There are about 2.3 million American Financial Enterprises common shares shares that American Financial Group does not own.

American Financial Group, a specialty and multiline property and casualty insurance company, said the cash to be used in the proposed deals will come from its internal resourcs and existing credit lines.

It said it will ask its shareholders to approve a plan or reorganization in which it would become the holding company for American Financial Corp and all of its subsidiaries. The holding company would also issue all of the new sotck to be exchange for American Financial Entedrprises' common stock.

The proposed transactions are subject to negotaition of final documentation, aplproval by the boards of the three companies and the receipt of all required shareholder, stock exchange and regulatory aprpovals.
